findings.title: aside-collect retry step does not say where the resume output is captured
findings.body: Step 3 redirects stdout and stderr of `aside exec` to `<TMP>/<STAMP>-<NONCE>.out.txt` and `.err.txt` with literal paths. Step 7's retry command is `aside session resume <id> "..." < /dev/null`, with no stdout redirect. It then says to 'save its output as `<STAMP>-<slug>-<RNONCE>-retry.md`' and to 'parse again', but it never names the scratch input file for `parse_aside.py`. Give the retry the same literal redirect form (`> <TMP>/<STAMP>-<RNONCE>.out.txt 2> ...`). Then show the exact parse command with `--clean <vault>/raw/aside/<STAMP>-<slug>-<RNONCE>-retry.md`, so an agent does not invent a different route.

findings.title: Source-note `raw:` path reuses the `<slug>` placeholder with a different meaning
findings.body: In step 8, `S-<slug>` is the per-item slug derived from the title. The `raw:` frontmatter value `raw/aside/<STAMP>-<slug>-<nonce>.md` needs the collection slug from step 3. Both use the same placeholder name, so an agent could write the item slug into `raw:`. The resulting path would not exist, and the provenance check ("a `raw` path that exists") would fail. Rename one placeholder, for example `<run-slug>`.

findings.title: verification.md contradicts itself on `cargo test -p X` and pnpm/yarn forms
findings.body: The plain-forms list counts `cargo test|clippy|build [--all|--workspace|-p X]` as normal evidence. The next bullet lists `cargo test ... -p X` as 'Filtered', meaning it is not evidence for the default rule. The summary line names `npm/pnpm/yarn test|lint|build|typecheck`, but the plain-forms list gives only `npm test` / `npm run ...`. Make the two lists agree with the runner allowlist in evidence.py, so Plan authors do not write a requirement that cannot be satisfied.

findings.title: maeng-archive --world eta is not tied to the eta/ vault folder
findings.body: SKILL.md says eta material is archived with `--world eta`, is kept under `eta/` and must never be mixed with personal archive paths. `cmd_move` does not check this. It accepts `--world personal` for `eta/...` paths and `--world eta` for any other path, and a stub written with `--world personal` gets no `world` key. Either reject a world/path mismatch or state that the agent has to choose the world correctly.
